study type: Retrospective cohort study using national registry data
cohort: The study cohort consisted of pregnant women and their infants identified from national birth registry data in Ecuador, comparing Venezuelan immigrants and Colombian immigrants with Ecuadorian nationals.
finding: Venezuelan and Colombian immigrants in Ecuador had different patterns of maternal care and experienced higher adjusted odds of adverse infant outcomes, including preterm birth and low birthweight, compared to Ecuadorian nationals.
mod_finding: Both Venezuelan and Colombian immigrants had increased adjusted odds for institutional and C-section deliveries compared to Ecuadorian nationals.
